amber-ghost.note: Inlined as %23282010 in the matrix ghost-grid SVG data URI; change both together.

engrave.note: White at 60% alpha; the ramp is the neutral white axis.

amber-rim.purpose: The rim of a lit lamp, 3:1 and more against aluminium.

field-edge.purpose: Sides and bottom of a paper field's sunk well.

field-edge-top.purpose: Top wall of a paper field's sunk well.

display.purpose: The maker's plate in the rail; one per page. Uppercase.

headline.purpose: Engraved panel headings (State, Questions, Raw exchange). Uppercase.

title.purpose: A channel's question id, shown exactly as in the request.

body.purpose: Running text and option names (500 for option names); tabular numerals throughout.

body-small.purpose: Channel instructions (max 65ch); 0.875rem variant for notes and level-fit lines.

label.purpose: Engraved legends under and beside every control and window. Uppercase, 1px engrave under-shadow.

key-legend.purpose: The RUN transport key's legend. Uppercase.

switch.purpose: The model name on the chrome model switch.

figure.purpose: Returned text values (the chosen answer), amber on glass.

code.purpose: The state tape and questions editor.

matrix.purpose: Dot-matrix counters (latency, tokens); 1.375rem at phone width.

matrix-readout.purpose: Per-option percent readouts and figure readouts; 1.125rem at phone width.

shadows.name: engraving
shadows.purpose: text-shadow: legends and headings cut into aluminium; dropped on paper and the dark shell.

shadows.name: groove
shadows.purpose: The two-line rule under the rail and panel heads (inset variant above the figures row); replaces every divider.

shadows.name: channel-module
shadows.purpose: Bolted question modules raised off the fascia.

shadows.name: key-rest
shadows.purpose: RUN key only: the 3px skirt is the key's travel.

shadows.name: key-pressed
shadows.purpose: RUN key pressed or busy, with translateY(3px).

shadows.name: sunk-window-bevel
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: the border bevel that sinks every glass window (3px top for the larger wells).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing: key press and ladder climb.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: RUN key transform and shadow transition; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: ladder-climb
motion.purpose: Lit ladder segments climb from zero to the returned level via clip-path; static under reduced motion.

components.name: RUN Transport Key
components.description: The only transport key: a chrome transport key with an LED strip; pressing or running drops it 3px and burns the strip amber. Held with aria-disabled, never disabled; a Changed lamp beneath lights while the inputs differ from the last run. While a run waits on its model's first download the legend reads Pulling, and a Soft Engraving note under the rail says what is downloading and its size; no progress bar is drawn.

narrative.overview:
The playground is one piece of consumer hardware: a brushed-aluminium fascia set into a beige plastic surround, lit from above. The state loads into a dark cassette shell behind a paper label; each question is a bolted channel module; every option's probability climbs an amber LED ladder behind smoked glass and lands on a dot-matrix readout. Nothing on the fascia is decoration without a hardware reason: legends are engraved, windows are sunk, keys travel, and lamps are dark until something is live.

Density is instrument-panel density: small engraved caps under every control, generous module padding, and figures set large enough to read at a glance. The world is light-only (`color-scheme: light`); the beige surround and aluminium are the page, and the only dark surfaces are windows into the machine (glass, the cassette shell, the wire). The confirmed rejection is the two-pane API console of grey borders and a blue Run button: no flat grey rules, no blue, no generic primary button.

Amber is signal, not paint. It appears where the machine has something to say (a returned figure, the winning answer, the busy RUN strip) and nowhere else. Red is spent on faults only.
keyCharacteristics: Aluminium fascia on beige surround, lit from above; every surface has a light-from-above reason.
Engraved narrow-grotesk caps (Barlow Condensed) as the legend under or beside every control and window.
Smoked-glass windows with a sunk bevel for every live figure; amber dot-matrix numerals (Doto) inside.
Amber LED ladders on an 8px segment pitch with a quarter-tick scale beneath.
One pressable chrome transport key (RUN) with real key travel; every other key is a flat chrome plate that sits in when pressed.
Red reserved for faults; amber reserved for live signal.

rules.name: The Amber Is Live Rule
rules.body: Amber marks live signal only: returned figures, the winning answer's lamp and underline, the busy RUN strip, the lit lamp of the state mode, of a pressed toggle key (what will be sent) and of the Changed lamp (the inputs differ from the last run), selection and the tape's focus ring. It is never a border, a background panel, a heading colour or an ornament.

rules.name: The Red Is a Fault Rule
rules.body: The three fault colours appear only when a request or input was refused. No red for emphasis, warnings or destructive-looking controls.

rules.name: The Unlit Is Not Text Rule
rules.body: Unlit Amber and Ghost Matrix sit at about 1.4:1 on glass by design; they draw dark dots and segments only. An idle window shows an empty cell with a visually hidden "not run yet" / "none yet", never dim digits.

rules.name: The Four Faces Rule
rules.body: Each face has one job: Barlow Condensed engraves, Barlow Semi Condensed reads, IBM Plex Mono is copied, Doto reports. Doto never sets words; Plex never sets legends.

rules.name: The Engraved Legend Rule
rules.body: Every control and every window carries a legend in the Label role, cut into the panel with a 1px Engrave Light under-shadow. On paper or on the dark shell the under-shadow is dropped, since there is no aluminium to cut into.

rules.name: The Doto Point Rule
rules.body: Doto's own full stop is a cross of dots that reads as "+". Every decimal point in a dot-matrix figure is set in its own span that keeps the glyph cell transparent and seats one square dot (0.085em on the 0.1em pitch) on the baseline, so the text stays exact and the point reads as a point.

rules.name: The Figures As Returned Rule
rules.body: Probabilities show as percent with one decimal; confidence, noul, score and extras with two decimals; counts and names verbatim. Each figure carries its raw value and JSON pointer, and no figure is restyled into something the API did not say.

rules.name: The Sunk Window Rule
rules.body: Every glass window (counters, readouts, figures, ladders, the wire, the cassette window) is sunk with a bevel border: top 2px (3px for the larger wells) Bevel Deep, sides 1px Bevel Side, bottom 1px Aluminium Highlight. Windows never cast shadows.

rules.name: The Key Travel Rule
rules.body: The 3px solid skirt under the RUN key is the key's travel, consumed when it is pressed or busy. It belongs to pressable transport keys only; nothing else gets a hard offset shadow.

dos: **Do** set every live figure in amber Doto inside a sunk Smoked Glass window over the ghost grid, and set decimal points with the Doto Point treatment.
**Do** engrave a Label legend (Barlow Condensed 600, 0.75rem, 0.12em, uppercase, 1px Engrave Light under-shadow) under or beside every control and window.
**Do** separate regions with the two-line Groove (Aluminium Shade over Aluminium Highlight), never a flat border.
**Do** light surfaces from above: white top highlights on raised parts, dark top walls on sunk windows.
**Do** keep motion to the RUN key press and the snap of plate and toggle keys (80ms) and the ladder climb (900ms), all on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` and all off under reduced motion.
**Do** keep the state on the left and the questions on the right; restack as console, cassette, channels, exchange, snippets in one column.
donts: **Don't** build the two-pane API console of grey borders and a blue Run button; no blue anywhere on the fascia.
**Don't** use amber for borders, panel fills, headings or decoration; it marks live signal only.
**Don't** use the fault reds for anything but a refused request or invalid input.
**Don't** put a readable figure in Unlit Amber or Ghost Matrix; idle windows are empty cells with hidden text.
**Don't** set words in Doto, legends in Plex, or prose in Barlow Condensed.
**Don't** give any surface other than a pressable transport key a hard offset shadow; plate keys and toggle keys sit in, they do not travel.
**Don't** round, restyle or re-derive a returned value; show it at the stated precision with its raw value attached.
